source.episode_title: Jesus Promised Paradise to a Criminal
source.hook_line: # Jesus Promised Paradise to a Criminal — Luke 23:39-43 Series: Words from the Cross · Cluster 1 (The Cross) · style: inked motion-comic (living page) · 38s sho
source.spoken_script: # Jesus Promised Paradise to a Criminal — Luke 23:39-43 Series: Words from the Cross · Cluster 1 (The Cross) · style: inked motion-comic (living page) · 38s short Note: deliberate clause-boundary partials, tagged on screen — Luke 23:39b (mocker), 23:42b (other thief), 23:43b (Jesus). KJV "To day" spelling preserved. Verses 40-41 are not quoted. Words LOCKED 2026-11-09. [narrator] Jesus promised paradise to a criminal. Why? [narrator] Two criminals were dying on crosses beside Him. [mocker] If thou be Christ, save thyself and us. [narrator] One wanted off the cross. The other asked for very little. [penitent] Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom. [narrator] He asked to be remembered. Someday. [jesus] To day shalt thou be with me in paradise. [narrator] Not someday. Today. Not just remembered. With Him. You can ask Him to remember you too.

redteam:
VERDICT: REVISE

- YouTube (Long-form 16:9), title "...explained simply" and description "This is the long-form companion to the short": the narration is a 38s short only. Nothing in the source supports a long-form film, and "explained" promises teaching the short does not deliver. Fix: drop the long-form kit unless a real long-form film exists. If one does, write it from that script, not a copy of the short's copy.
- YouTube (Short) title "...why Jesus promised him paradise | Bible": the video asks "Why?" but never states a reason. It only shows the thief asked to be remembered and Jesus said "Today" and "with Me". Verses 40-41 (his fear of God, "we receive the due reward of our deeds", "this man hath done nothing amiss") are explicitly not quoted. So "why" is a gap with a thin payoff. Fix: reword to what the video delivers, e.g. "He asked to be remembered. Jesus said 'Today.' | Luke 23". Or keep the title and make the first description line say the answer in plain words ("because he asked Jesus").
- The same title ends in a generic "| Bible" tag. It adds no information and the "famous neighbour" is already in the first words. Fix: replace with "| Luke 23:43".
- YouTube (Short) and Facebook descriptions start with "Bible: two criminals die beside Jesus." The "Bible:" prefix is a template tic and weakens the first line (it is what shows in the fold). Fix: open with "Two criminals die beside Jesus. One mocks. One asks to be remembered."
- YouTube (Short) description, 'Jesus said to him, "To day shalt thou be with me in paradise." (Luke 23:43, KJV)': the quoted words are verbatim, but the lead-in "Jesus said to him" is not KJV ("And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, To day..."), and the "KJV" tag sits right after it. Fix: write 'Jesus said unto him, "...To day shalt thou be with me in paradise."' or mark the quote as partial.
- All platforms, "He asked for very little": this is the video's own line, but it is a loose claim. He asked for entry into the kingdom, which is not little. The video leans on it as irony, but the copy states it with no frame. Fix: add "...and got far more", or quote the actual request in the description (Luke 23:42b, "Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.", verbatim KJV).
- TikTok / Facebook / Instagram, "Send this to someone who thinks it is too late for them": the video never says "too late". It ends on "You can ask Him to remember you too." The line is a shareable, grace-consistent hook, but it is slightly off-thread and could be read as a deathbed-conversion promise to anyone. Fix: "Send this to someone who needs to hear Today, not someday." That matches the video's own turn ("Not someday. Today.").
- Tags "penitent thief" and "thief on the cross": the Luke text says "malefactors/criminals" and the video says "criminal". The video also never shows his repentance (vv.40-41 cut). This is common search wording, so acceptable. Keep, but do not put "penitent" in any visible copy.
- Instagram: 8 hashtags, with #Faith and #Gospel generic. Trim to 4-5 that match the story (#ThiefOnTheCross #Luke23 #Jesus #BibleStory).
- Positive: the KJV quotes checked out (23:39b, 23:42b, 23:43b are verbatim substrings). The AI disclosure is not in the kit. If the channel policy needs the honest AI note, it is missing from every platform.
